Contains a legible carved ground threshold and a usable void condition
Best aligns with the required active edge plus public void language
Second distinct family with a different overall silhouette from the slab/bar type
Upper body reads as a curved/profiled prism, which adds some family variety

rationale: The contact sheet only shows 2 of 20 silhouette-distinct masses, so the portfolio cannot pass as a 20-option set. The two visible candidates are both compact and program-adjacent, but they still cluster around a similar bar/prism logic with repeated entry-notch behavior, and neither demonstrates a broad enough spread of spatial families to satisfy the ten-family minimum or the under-30% dominant-family rule at portfolio scale. The brief calls for a compact street building with active ground edge, one clear public void/terrace, and calm upper massing; these qualities are only partially legible here and need to be expanded through more varied sectional and threshold relations rather than more small outline tweaks.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: voided slab with frontage entry notch and bend; rectilinear bar family with carved ground and recursive void roof
profiled prism with frontage entry notch and rounded/inflated upper body; compact bar-to-prism family with similar ground cut

required_next_relations: Add at least 8 more materially different families so the set reaches 10+ legible massing types
Use distinct macro-operators across the set: courtyard, notch, setback, terrace, cantilever, bridge, cross_mass, bent_bar, split_wing, puncture, cut_corner, stepped_mass
Create one clearly public void or terrace that is larger and more legible than decorative subtraction
Maintain a calm upper mass while varying the ground threshold and section relationship
Introduce some access-bound relations that explicitly show west-side street entry and public-to-private transition
Avoid repeating the same slab/bar footprint and avoid repeated roof caps or pyramidal/box families
Differentiate by section logic, not just outline edits: lift, split, attach_volume, carve_void, and stepped transitions should each produce a clearly different spatial reading
